proposed.explanation:
COMI (Commercial International Bank of Egypt) shows strong fundamental growth that aligns well with your high-growth, 10-year horizon profile. Key signals from the FY2025 condensed consolidated report:

• Loan book grew ~48% YoY (from 343.5 bn EGP to 508.0 bn EGP), indicating aggressive credit expansion and a leading indicator of future earnings.
• Net interest income rose ~18% YoY (from 91.1 bn to 107.7 bn EGP), confirming the loan growth is translating into revenue.
• Basic EPS grew ~24% YoY (from 14.72 to 18.25 EGP per share), showing solid earnings momentum.
• At 128 EGP per share, the implied P/E is roughly 7×, which is not expensive for a bank growing EPS at 24%.

Given your high risk tolerance, no liquidity needs, and 10-year horizon, initiating a position in a bank with this growth trajectory is reasonable. I am limited to 58 shares (7,424 EGP) by the diversification rule: no single holding may exceed 50% of total portfolio value (15,000 EGP). After the purchase you will hold 7,424 EGP in COMI (49.5%) and 7,576 EGP in cash.

Risks and caveats: We only have one year of comparative data (FY2024 vs FY2025). There is no evidence on capital adequacy, non-performing loan ratios, or the full income statement. A 48% jump in loans could reflect aggressive underwriting that may later surface as credit losses. Banking is also sensitive to interest-rate and regulatory shifts. This is a single-company position in a single sector; the remaining cash should ideally be deployed into other sectors over time to build a more diversified portfolio. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
